messages.claude:
fix masking and rnn mask shape handling across backends (#1567)

The Masking layer produced masks with the wrong rank, which broke K.rnn
on both tensorflow and theano backends. Masks were being computed with an
extra trailing axis (samples, time, 1) instead of (samples, time), so
dimshuffle/transpose failed when the recurrent layer tried to align the
mask with the time axis.

What:
- Masking.get_output_mask now returns a 2D mask via K.not_equal, and
  get_output casts the boolean mask to floatx before multiplying.
- Embedding.get_output_mask drops the spurious expand_dims so masks stay
  2D.
- tensorflow_backend.rnn expands a 2D mask to 3D before transposing it
  (bool tensors cannot be transposed directly, so the uint8 round-trip
  is kept), and any() now returns uint8 to match.
- theano_backend.rnn asserts/expand_dims the mask to the expected ndim
  before dimshuffle.
- objectives.categorical_crossentropy no longer averages over the last
  axis (so masking keeps per-step losses), and cosine_proximity uses
  axis=-1 and drops the 2D ndim assertions.
- Removed the tensorflow-skip markers from the masking/rnn tests and
  added test_masking_layer + test_objectives to lock in the fix.

Why: Issue #1567 reported a ValueError when stacking Masking + LSTM
because K.rnn assumed a 3D mask while the Masking layer emitted a mask
with a trailing dimension. Aligning mask rank across Masking, Embedding
and both backends resolves the crash and lets masked recurrent models
train end-to-end on tensorflow as well as theano.
messages.kimi:
fix: Fix masking dimension handling in K.rnn and Masking layer (#1567)

Fix incorrect mask shape assumptions causing ValueError when using Masking layer with RNNs. The issue was that K.rnn expected 3D masks but Masking layer produced 2D masks.

Changes:
- Update `any()` to return uint8 instead of int8 for consistency
- Fix mask shape handling in TensorFlow backend rnn() to support both 2D and 3D masks
- Fix mask shape handling in Theano backend rnn() with proper dimension expansion
- Simplify Masking layer implementation using K.not_equal() and proper casting
- Fix Embedding layer mask output shape (remove unnecessary expand_dims)
- Fix categorical_crossentropy to not reduce over last axis (match expected behavior)
- Fix cosine_proximity to use axis=-1 for multi-dimensional support
- Remove TensorFlow skip markers from masking tests now that fixes are in place
- Add comprehensive tests for masking layer with RNNs and objective function shapes
messages.minimax:
Fix masking issues in RNN and Masking layer for TensorFlow and Theano backends

The Masking layer was producing masks with inconsistent dimensionality compared to what K.rnn expected, causing dimension mismatch errors when used with LSTM/GRU layers. This commit addresses several related issues: the any() function returned int8 instead of uint8; the RNN backends did not handle masks with ndim-1 dimensions; the Masking layer's get_output_mask removed dimensions inconsistently; and categorical_crossentropy and cosine_proximity had axis parameter bugs. Tests previously skipped for TensorFlow are now re-enabled, and a new test validates the fix against issue #1567.

Issue #1768: Bug in callbacks.py ModelCheckpoint class
There is a bug in the constructor of the ModelCheckpoint class (lines 247-259)

See code below (from master branch). If the mode parameter is not recognized, the warning message refers to a self.mode variable that is never initialized, and an exception is thrown:

`AttributeError: 'ModelCheckpoint' object has no attribute 'mode'`

--- Code from callbacks.py ---

```
 def __init__(self, filepath, monitor='val_loss', verbose=0,
                 save_best_only=False, mode='auto'):


        super(Callback, self).__init__()
        self.monitor = monitor
        self.verbose = verbose
        self.filepath = filepath
        self.save_best_only = save_best_only

        if mode not in ['auto', 'min', 'max']:
            warnings.warn('ModelCheckpoint mode %s is unknown, '
                          'fallback to auto mode.' % (self.mode),
                          RuntimeWarning)
```

messages.kimi:
fix: Fix AttributeError in ModelCheckpoint warning message

Fix the warning message in ModelCheckpoint.__init__ to use the local 'mode' parameter instead of 'self.mode' which hasn't been assigned yet. When an invalid mode is passed, the warning would raise AttributeError because self.mode doesn't exist at that point in the constructor.
messages.claude:
fix: use `mode` instead of `self.mode` in ModelCheckpoint warning

The ModelCheckpoint constructor references `self.mode` in the
warning message emitted when the `mode` argument is not one of
'auto', 'min', or 'max'. At this point `self.mode` has not been
assigned yet, so the warning itself raises `AttributeError:
'ModelCheckpoint' object has no attribute 'mode'`, masking the
intended invalid-mode warning (see issue #1768). Reference the
local `mode` parameter instead so the warning is constructed
before the attribute exists and the fallback to 'auto' proceeds
as designed.
messages.minimax:
fix: correct mode reference in ModelCheckpoint warning message

When an invalid mode is passed to ModelCheckpoint, the warning message referenced self.mode before it was initialized, causing an AttributeError. Fixed by using the mode parameter directly.

messages.kimi:
feat: Implement border_mode="same" support for pool2d in Theano backend

Implement padding logic for border_mode="same" in the pool2d function, enabling AveragePooling2D and MaxPooling2D layers to use "same" padding with the Theano backend. Previously, this raised a NotImplementedError. The implementation calculates appropriate padding based on pool_size parity and crops the output to match expected dimensions, aligning Theano backend behavior with TensorFlow.
messages.minimax:
Add border_mode='same' support for Pooling2D with Theano backend

Implement border_mode='same' padding for pooling operations in the Theano backend, addressing issue #1763. Previously, Theano's pool2d raised an exception when border_mode='same' was specified. The implementation calculates appropriate padding based on pool size and strides, and crops the output to match the expected output shape when border_mode='same'.
messages.claude:
feat: add border_mode="same" support for Theano pool2d

Previously, calling pool2d with border_mode="same" on the Theano
backend raised a NotImplementedError, forcing users to work around
the limitation. This was raised in issue #1763, where it was noted
that Theano's downsample.max_pool_2d already accepts a padding
argument, so supporting "same" should be straightforward.

This change computes asymmetric padding based on pool_size so that
the output spatial dimensions match the input when strides==(1, 1).
Odd pool sizes use pool_size - 2, even sizes use pool_size - 1, which
yields the correct output size after Theano's max_pool_2d and the
subsequent crop to the expected (ceil(input/stride)) shape. For
strides > 1 the output is cropped to the expected width/height so
the result is consistent across stride configurations.

ignore_border is now always set to True, since the previous
differentiation only existed to support the "same" path that raised
before.

Tests for AveragePooling2D are extended to cover both 'valid' and
'same' border modes across multiple pool sizes and strides, and to
assert that input and output shapes match for strides==(1, 1) under
'same' padding.

context.issue:
Issue #2287: Add option to change generator queue size in fit_generator
I'm training a 3D CNN model on video clips and my batch generator is eating up all the memory on my machine. I see that the `generator_queue` function has a `max_q_size` argument, but there's no way to set it in the `fit_generator` call.

Here's [a link](https://gist.github.com/jbencook/15cd39799dbefdccae9c4087647a5f91) to my code, which works until I run out of memory. I'm using the data described [here](https://github.com/gtoderici/sports-1m-dataset).

messages.claude:
feat: expose max_q_size parameter in fit_generator, evaluate_generator and predict_generator

Previously the generator_queue function already accepted a max_q_size
argument, but it was hardcoded to the default value of 10 inside
fit_generator, evaluate_generator and predict_generator, with no way for
users to override it.

This became a real problem when training data-heavy models (e.g. 3D CNNs
on video clips, as reported in #2287): the default queue size of 10
causes the generator thread to pre-fetch and hold many batches in
memory, exhausting system RAM before training even gets going. Users had
no recourse other than monkey-patching the internal queue call.

This change threads a max_q_size parameter through the public API of
fit_generator, evaluate_generator and predict_generator (in both
keras/engine/training.py and keras/models.py) and passes it down to
generator_queue. The docstrings and the generator_queue comment are
updated to reflect that predict_generator also uses the shared queue
helper. Tests are extended to exercise a non-default max_q_size value.

Closes #2287.
messages.kimi:
feat: Add max_q_size parameter to fit_generator, evaluate_generator, and predict_generator (#2287)

This change exposes the `max_q_size` parameter to users of `fit_generator`, `evaluate_generator`, and `predict_generator` methods. Previously, the `generator_queue` function had a `max_q_size` argument, but there was no way to configure it from the public API. This caused memory issues for users training 3D CNN models on video clips where the batch generator would consume all available memory. Users can now control the generator queue size to better manage memory usage based on their specific hardware constraints and data requirements.
messages.minimax:
Add max_q_size parameter to generator methods (#2287)

Allow configuring the generator queue size in `fit_generator`, `evaluate_generator`, and `predict_generator` to prevent memory exhaustion when training on large datasets. Previously the queue size was fixed at 10, causing OOM errors with heavy batch generators.

Issue #2297: TensorBoard with Histograms crashes with Dropout Layers
The most recent version of Keras crashes after the first epoch when a TensorBoard callback is added that records histograms.

Failing Example Code (`examples/mnist_mlp.py` with added callback) and Crash Log:
https://gist.github.com/jdoerrie/713a2d53e14b01470aa664494186d7c7

Judging by the output the issue is related to `keras_learning_phase` not being fed. The code works normally when `histogram_freq` is set to 0 or the Dropout layers are removed.
- Operating System: Mac OS X 10.11.3
- Python: 3.5.1
- Keras: 1.0.0 (Master Checkout)
- Tensorflow: 0.7.1
- Running on CPU.

messages.kimi:
fix: Fix TensorBoard histogram crash with Dropout layers (#2297)

The TensorBoard callback was crashing when recording histograms in models with Dropout layers because the `keras_learning_phase` placeholder was not being fed during the validation data session run. This change detects when the model uses learning phase (e.g., for Dropout/BatchNormalization) and includes the learning phase tensor (set to 0 for test mode) in the feed_dict, ensuring proper behavior during histogram computation.
messages.claude:
fix: feed learning phase to TensorBoard histogram callback

When a model uses learning phase (e.g. contains Dropout layers), the
TensorBoard callback's on_epoch_end builds a feed_dict from only
model.inputs and validation_data, omitting the learning_phase placeholder
that such models add to their input list. This caused the session.run
call to crash after the first epoch with histograms enabled, since
TensorFlow could not feed keras_learning_phase.

Pass the learning_phase tensor (with value 0 for inference) into the
feed_dict when the model depends on it, leaving the non-learning-phase
path unchanged.

Also re-enable the test_TensorBoard test under Python 3 and switch the
__main__ entry point to run the full test module via pytest instead of
only the TensorBoard test, ensuring the callback path is exercised.
messages.minimax:
Fix TensorBoard histogram crash with Dropout layers

When histogram_freq > 0, the session.run call requires the learning_phase
tensor to be included in the feed dict for models that use_learning_phase.
Without it, the callback crashes after the first epoch.

Fixes #2297

Issue #2498: save optimizer and objective information to configure file
It seems that keras 1 doesn't support save optimizer and loss to configure file any more. It there some alternative way? Or any plan to add this function back again?

messages.kimi:
feat: Add Keras version, optimizer, and loss information to model serialization

Add `_updated_config()` method to consolidate model configuration serialization logic across `to_json()` and `to_yaml()`. The method includes Keras version, optimizer configuration, loss function name, sample weight mode, and loss weights in the serialized output.

This addresses issue #2498 where users needed to save optimizer and objective information to configuration files. Previously, this information was lost during serialization, making it impossible to fully reconstruct a compiled model from its saved configuration. The change ensures model state can be properly persisted and restored.
messages.claude:
feat: save optimizer, loss, and loss_weights info to model config

Extract a shared `_updated_config()` helper used by `to_json` and `to_yaml` to serialize the model. The new config augments `get_config()` output with keras version, optimizer config, loss name, sample_weight_mode, and loss_weights (the latter now stored on the model in `compile`).

Why: Keras 1 stopped persisting optimizer and loss information into the serialized model config, leaving users no way to recover the training setup from a saved configuration (issue #2498). By reusing the existing serialization paths (`to_json`/`to_yaml`) and recording the keras version alongside the optimizer/loss metadata, saved configs become self-describing and round-trippable across versions. Consolidating the duplicated config construction into `_updated_config()` keeps `to_json` and `to_yaml` consistent and avoids drift between the two formats.
messages.minimax:
feat: add optimizer and loss serialization to model config

Serialize optimizer config, loss class name, loss_weights, and keras_version when saving model to JSON/YAML. This restores the ability to save and restore complete model compilation state that was lost in Keras 2.x, addressing issue #2498.

Issue #2864: KerasClassifier does not return the same thing as scikit learn in the case of binary classification
For binary classification using a stock classifier from scikit, running predict_proba will return a matrix of shape (n_samples,n_classes) however KerasClassifier returns (nsamples,noutputs).

This results in the inability to use the ootb cross_val_score with 'roc_auc' due to the error:

```
site-packages\sklearn\metrics\scorer.pyc in __call__(self, clf, X, y, sample_weight)
    173 
    174                 if y_type == "binary":
--> 175                     y_pred = y_pred[:, 1]
    176                 elif isinstance(y_pred, list):
    177                     y_pred = np.vstack([p[:, -1] for p in y_pred]).T
IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 1
```

messages.claude:
fix: return 2-column probability matrix for binary classification in KerasClassifier.predict_proba (#2864)

scikit-learn's predict_proba contract returns an (n_samples, n_classes)
matrix, even for binary classification where it yields two columns
(P(class=0), P(class=1)). KerasClassifier instead returned an
(n_samples, 1) matrix containing only P(class=1), which broke
cross_val_score with the 'roc_auc' scorer: the scorer does
y_pred[:, 1] for binary tasks and raises
"IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 1".

Detect the single-output binary case (probs.shape[1] == 1) and
horizontally stack [1 - probs, probs] to produce the expected
(n_samples, 2) layout, mirroring sklearn's behavior. Also document
the returned shape in the docstring.
messages.kimi:
fix: Make KerasClassifier.predict_proba return (n_samples, 2) for binary classification

KerasClassifier.predict_proba() was returning shape (n_samples, 1) for binary
classification, but scikit-learn expects (n_samples, n_classes) i.e.
(n_samples, 2). This caused IndexError when using cross_val_score with
'roc_auc' scorer, which accesses y_pred[:, 1].

The fix detects binary classification (single output column) and stacks
the complementary probabilities to match scikit-learn's expected output
format, enabling compatibility with standard sklearn metrics and
cross-validation utilities.
messages.minimax:
Fix KerasClassifier.predict_proba shape for binary classification

KerasClassifier.predict_proba was returning shape (n_samples, 1) for binary
classification while sklearn returns (n_samples, 2). This caused
cross_val_score with 'roc_auc' to fail with IndexError because the scorer
expects to access y_pred[:, 1].

The fix detects single-column output and stacks [1-probs, probs] to
produce (n_samples, 2), matching sklearn's API and restoring cross_val_score
compatibility.

feat: Add GlobalAveragePooling3D and GlobalMaxPooling3D layers

Add 3D global pooling layers to support pooling operations on 5D tensors (samples, dimensions..., channels). This implements the feature requested in issue #3942, which noted the absence of 3D versions of global pooling layers despite having 2D variants.

The implementation includes:
- Base class `_GlobalPooling3D` with dimension ordering support ('th'/'tf')
- `GlobalAveragePooling3D`: computes mean across spatial dimensions
- `GlobalMaxPooling3D`: computes max across spatial dimensions
- Comprehensive tests for both 'th' and 'tf' dimension orderings
messages.claude:
feat: add GlobalAveragePooling3D and GlobalMaxPooling3D layers

Add 3D global pooling operations (GlobalAveragePooling3D and
GlobalMaxPooling3D) to keras/layers/pooling.py, along with a shared
_GlobalPooling3D base class that mirrors the structure of the existing
2D variants.

The new layers accept 5D tensors and reduce the three spatial dimensions,
supporting both 'th' and 'tf' dim_ordering conventions just like their 2D
counterparts. Corresponding tests are added in
tests/keras/layers/test_convolutional.py covering both ordering modes and
both pooling kinds.

Why: Keras offered GlobalMaxPooling2D/GlobalAveragePooling2D but had no 3D
equivalents, forcing users working with volumetric inputs (e.g. video or 3D
medical scans) to either reshape and reuse the 2D layers or implement custom
ops. As noted in issue #3942, the 2D implementation already provided the
template; exposing the 3D analogues removes that gap and keeps the pooling API
consistent across input dimensionalities.

messages.claude:
fix: make backend functions respect set_floatx() at call time (#3891)

Previously, the default dtype for backend functions (variable, placeholder, zeros, ones, eye, random_*, etc.) was bound to the module-level _FLOATX constant, which was captured once at import time. As a result, calling set_floatx() after import had no effect on tensors created through these functions, breaking the documented behavior of switching the global float type at runtime.

Replace the static _FLOATX default with a None sentinel and resolve the actual dtype via floatx() inside each function body, so the current global value is read at call time. The same change is applied to the conv pre/post-processing helpers and the var/mean bool-cast paths, which previously compared against _FLOATX directly. Theano backend is updated symmetrically.

Adds tests in tests/keras/backend/test_backends.py covering:
- set_floatx rejecting invalid values
- set_floatx accepting float16/float32/float64
- variable() honoring the current global floatx() (the original bug repro)
messages.kimi:
feat: Make backend functions respect dynamic floatx() changes

Replace static _FLOATX default parameter values with dynamic floatx() calls in TensorFlow and Theano backends. This fixes the issue where set_floatx() had no effect on variable creation after import because functions captured the initial _FLOATX value at definition time rather than checking the current float type at runtime.

The change ensures that dtype=None defaults trigger a live floatx() lookup, making the global float type setting actually mutable as intended.
messages.minimax:
Fix set_floatx not taking effect in backend functions

The backends were using the _FLOATX constant (evaluated once at import time) as the default dtype parameter for functions like variable(), placeholder(), zeros(), ones(), etc. This meant changes to the global float type via set_floatx() had no effect after import because the default value was already baked in.

Now these functions default to dtype=None and call floatx() at runtime to get the current global float type, ensuring set_floatx() changes are properly reflected. Similarly, internal checks like `_FLOATX == 'float64'` in conv/preprocess functions now use dtype(x) or floatx() to respect the current setting. Tests added to verify set_floatx correctly updates dtype for newly created variables.

messages.claude:
docs: fix causal Conv1D padding docstring to reflect that output[t] depends on input[t]

The previous docstring stated that with "causal" padding, output[t] depends
solely on input[:t-1], which is incorrect. The implementation shows that
output[t] always depends on input[t] (and earlier inputs), not exclusively
on inputs strictly before t. This change rewords the description to
"output[t] does not depend on input[t+1:]", which correctly conveys the
causality property without implying that input[t] itself is excluded.

This resolves issue #5942, which reported the mismatch between the
documented behavior and the actual implementation of causal padding in
Conv1D.

Fix for layers.Reshape when using -1 and a dynamic batch size. (#18792)

When using `-1` for one of the dimensions and a dynamic batch size, with the Tensorflow backend, in non eager mode, this would result in Tensors with a `None` dimension where the `-1` was. This is because the `reshape` op does not treat the batch size specially and therefore has no way to determine what goes to the batch dimension vs. the `-1` dimension.

To fix this, we resolve the `-1` to an actual number at build time since the layer knows that the batch dimension is untouched.

Note that this bug would not affect the JAX and PyTorch backends because we inject a fake batch size when needed.

messages.kimi:
fix: Add name_scope to Bidirectional layer's build method to prevent duplicate weight names

The Bidirectional layer's `build()` method was creating weights for both forward and backward layers without proper name scoping, causing a "Name already exists" RuntimeError when saving models with multiple Bidirectional layers to HDF5 format. By wrapping each layer's build call in `K.name_scope()` using the layer's name, we ensure unique weight names are generated, resolving the HDF5 save conflict reported in issue #5820.
messages.claude:
fix: wrap Bidirectional layer build in name_scope to prevent HDF5 name collisions

When saving a model containing Bidirectional layers to HDF5, a
RuntimeError "Unable to create link (Name already exists)" was raised
(see #5820). The root cause is that the forward and backward sub-layers
were built without entering their respective name scopes, so the
weights they created ended up under identical names in the saved HDF5
group, causing a collision during save_weights_to_hdf5_group.

By wrapping each sub-layer's build() call in K.name_scope with the
sub-layer's own name, the variables are namespaced correctly and the
HDF5 group names become unique, resolving the save failure.
messages.minimax:

When saving a model with a Bidirectional layer to HDF5 format, h5py raises "RuntimeError: Unable to create link (Name already exists)" due to name conflicts between forward and backward sub-layers. Wrapping build calls with K.name_scope ensures unique layer names during serialization.

messages.kimi:
fix: Add `custom_objects` parameter to `Sequential.from_config` to support custom layer deserialization

The `Sequential.from_config` method was missing the `custom_objects` parameter, preventing users from loading Sequential models containing custom layers even when providing the `custom_objects` argument to `load_model()`. This change passes the `custom_objects` parameter through to `layer_module.deserialize()`, enabling proper deserialization of custom layers in Sequential models and resolving the `ValueError: Unknown layer` error reported in issue #5956.
messages.claude:
feat: support custom_objects in Sequential.from_config

Add a `custom_objects` argument to `Sequential.from_config` and pass it
through to `layer_module.deserialize` when reconstructing each layer.

Why: `Sequential` models containing custom layers could be saved to
config but not restored from it. Issue #5956 reports that
`load_model(..., custom_objects={...})` raises `ValueError: Unknown
layer` for custom layers, because `from_config` did not accept or
forward `custom_objects` — it was silently dropped in
`generic_utils.deserialize`, so custom layer classes were never visible
during reconstruction. Propagating `custom_objects` from the loader
into the per-layer deserialize call fixes the round-trip and lets users
load `Sequential` models that reference user-defined layer classes.
messages.minimax:
fix: pass custom_objects to from_config for Sequential models with custom layers

When loading a Sequential model containing custom layers via `from_config`, the `custom_objects` parameter was not being passed to `layer_module.deserialize`, causing `ValueError: Unknown layer` when attempting to restore models with custom layers. This change adds the `custom_objects` argument to `from_config` and forwards it during layer deserialization, enabling proper restoration of Sequential models that include custom layers.

messages.claude:
fix: correct inverted word filter in imdb/reuters load_data when oov_char=None

When `oov_char=None`, the dataset loader is supposed to drop out-of-vocabulary
tokens and retain only the in-range words. However, the condition
`w >= num_words or w < skip_top` kept exactly the opposite: it kept the
out-of-range words and discarded the in-range ones, effectively flipping the
filter bit.

This matches the bug reported in issue #3688, where `imdb.load_data(oov_char=None, num_words=200)` returned tokens with min value 200 instead of values below 200.

Flip the predicate to `skip_top <= w < num_words` so the in-range words are
preserved. Applied to both `keras/datasets/imdb.py` and `keras/datasets/reuters.py` since they share the same faulty logic.
messages.kimi:
Looking at the code changes and the related issue, I can see this is a bug fix for the IMDB and Reuters dataset loading functions.

Analysis:
- The original code `if w >= num_words or w < skip_top:` was keeping words that are OUTSIDE the valid range (above num_words OR below skip_top)
- The fix `if skip_top <= w < num_words:` correctly keeps words that are WITHIN the valid range (between skip_top and num_words)
- Issue #3688 confirms this was a bug where the logic was inverted - when `oov_char=None`, the filter was keeping the wrong words instead of filtering them out

Commit type: fix

fix: Correct word filtering logic in IMDB and Reuters datasets (#3688)

Fix inverted boolean logic in the word filtering condition when `oov_char=None`. messages.claude:

When a logs value is a string (e.g. logs['foo'] = 'bar'), CSVLogger's
handle_value treats it as an Iterable of characters and outputs

iterable, so the existing Iterable branch incorrectly maps over each
character.

The fix adds an explicit check for six.string_types before the Iterable
check, returning the string as-is. This resolves issue #6459, where
string-valued logs entries were being mangled in the CSV output column.

messages.kimi:
feat: Add gradient visualization support to TensorBoard callback

Add `write_grads` parameter to TensorBoard callback to enable visualization of gradient histograms in TensorBoard. This addresses issue #6215 where users wanted to monitor weight gradient distributions during training.

The implementation:
- Adds `write_grads` parameter (default False) to TensorBoard.__init__
- Computes gradients using model.optimizer.get_gradients() and logs them as histograms
- Fixes validation data handling to properly include targets and sample_weights for gradient computation
- Exposes total_loss, sample_weights, and targets attributes in Sequential model for gradient access
- Updates tests to verify the new functionality

This allows users to debug training dynamics by visualizing how gradients flow through different layers, helping identify vanishing/exploding gradient problems.
messages.claude:
feat: add gradient visualization support to TensorBoard callback

Add `write_grads` option to the TensorBoard callback to visualize weight
gradient histograms alongside the existing weight histograms, addressing
the request in issue #6215 for inspecting gradient distributions during
training.

The implementation surfaces `total_loss`, `sample_weights`, and `targets`
on the wrapped Model so the callback can compute gradients via
`optimizer.get_gradients(model.total_loss, weight)` and log them as
`{weight.name}_grad` histograms.

To make gradient evaluation work, the callback's feed dict construction in
`on_epoch_end` is reworked. Previously, only `model.inputs` (plus the
learning phase flag) were fed, which left the `targets` and
`sample_weights` placeholders unsatisfied and caused the
`output_sample_weights` placeholder error reported in the issue. The new
implementation feeds inputs, targets, and sample_weights together, and
appends the learning phase tensor only when the model actually uses it.
An `assert len(val_data) == len(tensors)` guards the pairing.

`_fit_loop` in `training.py` now builds `validation_data` consistently as
`val_x + val_y + val_sample_weights` (plus the learning phase scalar when
needed), matching the tensor list consumed by the callback. The previous
`val_x + [val_y, val_sample_weights]` shape did not match the new feed
dict structure and would have broken the assert.

Tests are updated to exercise `write_grads=True` on both the sequential
and convnet TensorBoard paths, and a new `test_CallbackValData` verifies
that callback validation data always carries x, y, and sample weights
for both `fit` and `fit_generator`.
messages.minimax:
Add write_grads option to TensorBoard for gradient histogram visualization

This commit adds a new `write_grads` parameter to the TensorBoard callback that enables
visualizing gradient distributions in TensorBoard (fixes issue #6215).

Technical changes:
- Added `write_grads` parameter to TensorBoard.__init__ and stored as instance attribute
- Added gradient histogram logging in set_model when `write_grads=True`
- Fixed validation_data handling to properly include sample_weights and learning_phase
- Added `total_loss`, `sample_weights`, and `targets` attributes to the callback model wrapper
- Added `test_CallbackValData` to verify validation_data format consistency

The original gradient visualization approach failed because targets and sample_weights
are defined as placeholders requiring proper feed_dict specification. This fix ensures
gradients are computed with correct inputs from validation_data.

messages.kimi:
feat: Support dynamic shapes in repeat_elements for variable-length inputs (#7410)

Replace the static shape validation with a dynamic shape implementation using tf.tile to handle None dimensions in the input tensor. This enables layers like UpSampling1D to work with variable-length sequences without requiring fully-defined input shapes.

The previous implementation raised a ValueError when the axis dimension was None. The new approach uses an auxiliary axis and tf.tile to repeat elements, then reshapes the result to maintain proper shape inference for both static and dynamic shapes.
messages.claude:
feat: support dynamic shapes in repeat_elements for variable-length inputs

Previously, `repeat_elements` raised a `ValueError` when the input tensor
had an undefined dimension along the repeat axis (i.e. `x.shape[axis]`
was `None`). This blocked layers such as `UpSampling1D` from operating
on variable-length inputs (issue #7410), where the temporal axis is
unknown at graph-construction time.

The fix adds a fallback path for dynamic shapes. When the repeat axis is
static, the original `tf.split` + `concatenate` approach is preserved.
When it is `None`, we instead use `tf.tile` on an auxiliary axis to
mimic `np.repeat`, then `tf.reshape` to merge the auxiliary axis back
into the target axis. This keeps the operation semantically equivalent
to `np.repeat` while allowing fully dynamic batch/time dimensions.

The accompanying test is updated to exercise the dynamic-shape branch
across all backends except CNTK, and the old assertion that required
TensorFlow to raise `ValueError` for undefined dimensions is removed,
since that behaviour is now intentionally supported.
messages.minimax:
feat: add dynamic shape support to repeat_elements for variable-length upsampling

The `repeat_elements` function previously raised a ValueError when the input tensor had an undefined dimension (None) along the repeat axis, breaking UpSampling1D and similar layers for variable-length sequences. This change implements dynamic shape handling using tf.tile to mimic np.repeat behavior, allowing elements to be repeated along an axis with None dimension. The fix enables UpSampling1D to work with variable-length inputs as described in issue #7410.

messages.claude:
fix: resolve KeyError in to_json when model has unused input layers

Issue #7164 reported a KeyError in to_json/to_yaml when a model declares
multiple inputs but one of them is never used to produce any of the
outputs (e.g. `Model(inputs=[a, b], outputs=c)` where `c` only depends on
`a`). In that case `b`'s node never ends up in `container_nodes`, so
when `get_config` tried to look up the input layer's node_key in
`node_conversion_map` via `new_node_index = node_conversion_map[node_key]`,
it raised `KeyError: 'input_2_ib-0'`.

Root cause: the node-key construction `layer.name + '_ib-' + str(node_index)`
was duplicated in seven places across topology.py, and the input/output
serialization in `get_config` unconditionally assumed that every declared
input/output layer had a node present in `container_nodes`.

Changes:
- Extract the duplicated node-key construction into a `_node_key(layer, node_index)`
  static method on Layer, centralizing the format and making it reusable.
- Replace all seven inline copies of the key construction with calls to
  `_node_key`, so the format lives in exactly one place.
- In `get_config`, when iterating `input_layers` and `output_layers`,
  skip any layer whose `_node_key` is not in `container_nodes` instead of
  crashing with a KeyError. This is the actual fix: unused inputs/outputs
  are now omitted from the serialized config rather than crashing.
- Add `test_saving_unused_layers_is_ok` covering the exact scenario from
  the issue: a model with two inputs where only one feeds the output,
  exercising both `save_model`/`load_model` (which go through
  `get_config`).

The `_node_key` refactor is not strictly necessary for the bug fix, but it
removes the duplication that allowed the input/output serialization paths to
drift from the traversal path in the first place, and makes future
node-key consumers consistent with `container_nodes`.
messages.kimi:
fix: handle unused input layers in model serialization (#7164)

Fix KeyError when calling to_json() on models with multiple inputs where
some inputs are not used in the outputs. The error occurred because
node_conversion_map only contained nodes present in container_nodes,
but input/output layer processing attempted to look up all nodes
unconditionally.

Changes:
- Add _node_key() static method to centralize node key generation
- Skip input/output nodes not in container_nodes during config serialization
- Add test case for saving models with unused input layers

Fixes #7164
messages.minimax:
fix: handle KeyError in get_config when model has unused input layers

When a model has multiple inputs where one input is not used in the outputs, calling to_json() would fail with KeyError because the code attempted to look up node_conversion_map entries for input layers that were not part of container_nodes.

This change:

- Adds guard checks to skip node_keys not in container_nodes when processing input_layers and output_layers in get_config, ensuring only nodes actually used by the model are serialized

messages.kimi:
fix: Fix model loading bug for shared layers at heterogeneous depths (#7682)

Fixed a bug where models with shared layers used at different depths could be saved but not loaded. The issue occurred in `process_node` where `continue` was used instead of `return`, causing the function to proceed with incomplete node processing when layers weren't yet available.

The fix changes `continue` to `return` in two places within `process_node`, ensuring that when a layer's inbound dependencies aren't ready, the node is properly deferred via `add_unprocessed_node` and revisited later when all dependencies are resolved.

Added a test case `test_layer_sharing_at_heterogenous_depth_with_concat` that reproduces the exact scenario from the issue: a model where a shared layer (dense_A) is used at different depths in the computation graph (through dense_B and dense_C paths), combined with a concatenate operation.
messages.claude:
fix: process unprocessed layer nodes instead of skipping them in model deserialization

When loading a model config, `process_node` skipped unprocessed inbound
layers by calling `continue` inside the for-loop over inbound layers.
This meant the layer never got re-queued for later processing, so its
inbound nodes were silently dropped when a required layer appeared later
in the config than the current layer — producing
`ValueError('Missing layer: ...')` for models that mix shared layers
across heterogenous depths (e.g. `concatenate([B(A(x)), A(C(x))])`).

Replace `continue` with `return` so that, when an inbound layer is not
yet created or its node is not yet available, the current layer is added
to the unprocessed list and skipped for now, allowing it to be retried
in a subsequent pass once dependencies are created.

This makes any serializable model deserializable, fixing issue #7682.
A regression test covering shared layers at heterogenous depths with a
concatenate merge layer is added.
messages.minimax:
Fix loading bug for shared layers with concatenation at heterogeneous depth (#7682)

When deserializing models with shared layers at heterogeneous depth involving concatenation, the `process_node` function was using `continue` instead of `return` after adding unprocessed nodes. This caused subsequent layer processing to fail, resulting in a "Missing layer" error during model loading. The fix ensures proper early return to allow the layer to be added and processed correctly.

messages.claude:
build(docker): add missing dependencies and fix source mount path

What:
- Add `bcolz` to conda install and `sklearn_pandas` via pip in Dockerfile
- Change Makefile volume mounts from `$(SRC):/src` to `$(SRC):/src/workspace`
- Allow `SRC` to be overridden via `?=` instead of hard-setting it

Why:
Resolves the "ImportError: No module named 'keras'" reported in #6750. The
root cause is a path collision inside the container: the Keras source tree
was being cloned into `/src` by the Dockerfile, but the Makefile also mounted
the host's source directory onto `/src`, shadowing the installed package.
Mounting the host source onto `/src/workspace` instead leaves the cloned (and
pip-installed) Keras tree intact at `/src`, so `import keras` resolves
correctly.

Adding `bcolz` and `sklearn_pandas` supplies transitive dependencies that
Keras tests/utilities expect but were missing from the image. Making `SRC`
overridable with `?=` lets users point the build at a custom source checkout
without editing the Makefile.

messages.kimi:
fix: Normalize device names in multi_gpu_model to handle TF device naming format

TensorFlow returns device names in the format '/device:CPU:0' and '/device:GPU:N', but multi_gpu_model was expecting '/cpu:0' and '/gpu:N'. This caused ValueError when checking device availability on systems with GPUs. The fix adds a _normalize_device_name() helper that strips the 'device:' prefix and converts to lowercase, ensuring consistent device name comparison between Keras and TensorFlow.
messages.claude:
fix: normalize device names in multi_gpu_model to match TF's naming convention (#8220)

TF exposes devices with the `/device:GPU:N` format (e.g.
`/device:CPU:0`, `/device:GPU:0`), but `multi_gpu_model` built its
target list using the legacy `/cpu:0` and `/gpu:N` format. The
membership check therefore always failed on recent TF versions,
raising a `ValueError` claiming the GPUs were unavailable even when
they were present (issues #8220, #8213).

Add a `_normalize_device_name` helper that lowercases the name and
strips the `device:` prefix, and apply it to the list returned by
`_get_available_devices()` before comparing it against the target
devices. This lets the existing `target_devices` entries match
either naming convention, so `multi_gpu_model` works again on
tensorflow-nightly-gpu and TF >= 1.4 where the `/device:GPU:N`
format is standard.
messages.minimax:
fix: normalize device names in multi_gpu_model to handle TF naming format mismatch

When calling `multi_gpu_model` with `gpus=N`, Keras expects devices in `/gpu:N` format but TensorFlow may return devices as `/device:GPU:N` depending on version/config. This causes a ValueError even when sufficient GPUs are available.

Added `_normalize_device_name` helper to standardize device name format before comparison, converting `/device:GPU:N` and similar variants to `/gpu:N`. Applied normalization to `available_devices` so the device presence check correctly matches target devices.

Fixes #8220, #8213.

messages.kimi:
fix: Add warning for trainable weights inconsistency when model.trainable is modified

Issue #8121 reported that changing model.trainable after compilation causes
discrepancies between the reported trainable weights count and the actual
collected trainable weights used during training. This leads to confusing
behavior where model.summary() shows different trainable params before and
after modifying trainable flags, even though the optimizer was configured
with the original state.

This fix introduces a _check_trainable_weights_consistency() method that
compares trainable_weights against _collected_trainable_weights and emits
a UserWarning when they differ. The check is called during _make_train_function()
and model.summary() to alert users when they've modified model.trainable
without calling model.compile() again.

Also extracts count_params() into a reusable utility function in
layer_utils.py to ensure consistent parameter counting across the codebase.
messages.claude:
fix: warn on trainable weights discrepancy when model.trainable is changed without recompile

Issue #8121 reported that modifying `model.trainable` after `model.compile()` causes `summary()` to display an inconsistent trainable parameter count. The root cause is that `_collected_trainable_weights` is cached at compile time and is not refreshed when `model.trainable` is toggled afterward, so the reported trainable count diverges from the actual trainable state of the model.

To surface this footgun to users, add a shared `count_params` helper in `layer_utils.py` (operating on `set(weights)` to dedupe shared weights) and reuse it from `Layer.count_params` and `print_summary`. Introduce `Model._check_trainable_weights_consistency()`, which compares the parameter count of `trainable_weights` against `_collected_trainable_weights` and emits a `UserWarning` on mismatch. The check is invoked from `_make_train_function` (covering `fit`/`evaluate`/`predict`) and from `print_summary`, so users are alerted on both the summary path and the training path. Recompiling the model reconciles the two lists and silences the warning, matching user expectations in the issue.

A regression test `test_trainable_weights_count_consistency` reproduces issue #8121 and asserts the warning fires on both `summary()` and `fit()` after toggling `model.trainable`, and that it no longer fires after a fresh `compile()`.
messages.minimax:
fix: warn when trainable weights count becomes inconsistent after modifying trainable

When `model.trainable` is modified after compilation without calling `compile()` again,
the trainable params count in `summary()` becomes incorrect because
`_collected_trainable_weights` (set during compilation) diverges from `trainable_weights`.

This adds a `_check_trainable_weights_consistency()` check that compares parameter counts
between `trainable_weights` and `_collected_trainable_weights`, raising a warning via
`warnings.warn()` when inconsistency is detected (e.g. during `summary()` or `fit()`).

Fixes issue #8121.

fix: Fix Bidirectional layer weight loading from CuDNN to non-CuDNN LSTM

The weight preprocessing logic for Bidirectional layers was incorrectly nested inside the `original_keras_version == '1'` check, preventing proper weight transformation when loading CuDNN-trained weights into non-CuDNN LSTM layers in Keras 2.x. This caused dimension mismatch errors when attempting to use GPU-trained models on CPU.

The fix moves the Bidirectional weight preprocessing outside the version check, ensuring weights are correctly split and processed for forward and backward layers regardless of Keras version. Added test coverage for the bidirectional case to prevent regression.

messages.claude:
fix: reuse validation generator queue in fit_generator (#8842)

Previously, fit_generator called evaluate_generator with the raw
validation_data on every epoch, which spawned a fresh enqueuer each
time. As reported in #8842, this caused the validation generator to be
re-queued from scratch every epoch instead of being consumed
incrementally: each epoch refilled max_queue_size on top of the
validation_steps actually needed, so the generator was accessed far more
times than necessary (e.g. ~25 pulls/epoch instead of 15 with the
default queue_size=10).

Build the validation enqueuer once, before the training loop, and pass
the already-queued validation_generator into evaluate_generator with
workers=0 so it drains the persistent queue rather than starting a new
one. Track val_enqueuer alongside the training enqueuer and stop both in
the finally block (nested so a failure stopping one does not skip the
other).

Add a regression test asserting the train and validation generators are
pulled only within the expected per-epoch range, for both generator and
Sequence validation inputs.
messages.kimi:
feat: Use enqueuer for validation generator in fit_generator

This change adds enqueuer support for validation data when using fit_generator with workers > 0. Previously, the validation generator would be accessed more times than expected because it was not using a queue mechanism like the training generator. By using OrderedEnqueuer for Sequence validation data and GeneratorEnqueuer for other generators, validation data is now prefetched in a separate thread/process, improving efficiency and ensuring the generator is only accessed the expected number of times (validation_steps per epoch). This fixes the issue where validation generators were being consumed excessively across epochs.
messages.minimax:
fix: properly manage validation generator queue in fit_generator

When using fit_generator with a Sequence/Generator for validation_data and workers > 0, the validation generator was not properly managed through an enqueuer like the training generator. This caused the queue to be refilled every epoch regardless of validation_steps, leading to unnecessary generator consumption.

The fix moves validation enqueuer management into the same try/finally block as the training enqueuer, ensuring validation generators are properly started/stopped and evaluate_generator uses the controlled validation_generator instead of the raw validation_data.

messages.claude:
feat: Add sample_weight support to KerasClassifier.fit()

KerasClassifier.fit() previously did not accept a sample_weight
argument, which caused scikit-learn estimators that rely on weighted
training — such as AdaBoostClassifier — to reject KerasClassifier
instances with "ValueError: KerasClassifier doesn't support
sample_weight" (see issue #8448).

Users attempting to wrap a Keras model inside AdaBoostClassifier
could not proceed past estimator validation, blocking common boosting
workflows built on top of Keras classifiers.

This change exposes an explicit sample_weight parameter on
KerasClassifier.fit() and forwards it into the underlying fit call via
kwargs, allowing sample weights to flow through from scikit-learn's
boosting machinery into Keras training. The accompanying test now
passes a sample_weight array to assert_classification_works, covering
the new code path.
messages.kimi:
feat: Add sample_weight support to KerasClassifier.fit()

Add sample_weight parameter to KerasClassifier.fit() method to enable
compatibility with scikit-learn ensemble methods like AdaBoostClassifier
that require sample weighting during training.

The change allows passing sample_weight directly to the fit method,
which is then forwarded to the underlying Keras model's fit call via
kwargs. This resolves the ValueError when using KerasClassifier with
AdaBoostClassifier and other meta-estimators that rely on sample weights
for boosting algorithms.

Updated the test to verify sample_weight functionality works correctly.

`from keras.preprocessing.text import Tokenizer

texts = ['Just any text.']

messages.kimi:
fix: Handle multi-character split strings in text_to_word_sequence (#9538)

Summary

Fix a crash in `text_to_word_sequence` when the `split` parameter contains more than one character. The previous implementation used `str.maketrans` which requires equal length arguments, causing a `ValueError` when `split` had multiple characters.

Details

The fix refactors the translation logic to handle three cases:
- Python 2 with unicode text: uses character-by-character translation dict
- Python 2 with byte strings and single-char split: uses `maketrans`
- Python 2 with byte strings and multi-char split: falls back to `str.replace` loop
- Python 3: uses dict-based `maketrans` which supports multi-char replacement values

Added test cases to verify multi-character split works for both regular and unicode strings.
messages.claude:
fix: support multi-character split in text_to_word_sequence

Summary

`text_to_word_sequence` crashed with `ValueError: the first two maketrans arguments must have equal length` whenever the `split` argument was longer than one character. The root cause was the assumption that `split` is a single character: the code built a translation map with `maketrans(filters, split * len(filters))`, which only works when `len(split) == 1`.

This was exercised by `Tokenizer(split="any")`, which delegates to `text_to_word_sequence` and therefore raised the exception reported in #9538.

The fix branches on `len(split)`:
- Python 2, unicode input: unchanged (uses `dict((ord(c), unicode(split)) for c in filters)`).
- Python 2, single-char `split`: uses `maketrans(filters, split * len(filters))`.
- Python 2, multi-char `split`: falls back to `text.replace(c, split)` for each filter char, since `maketrans` cannot map a single source char to a multi-char replacement.
- Python 3: builds `translate_dict = {c: split for c in filters}` and uses `str.translate`, which supports multi-char replacements natively.

Reasons

- `maketrans` requires its first two arguments to be of equal length, so it cannot translate a single source character into a multi-character string. This limitation made any tokeniser configured with a multi-character `split` (e.g. `Tokenizer(split="any")`) unusable, as reported in #9538.
- For Python 3, `str.translate` accepts a dict mapping single chars to arbitrary-length replacements, so the multi-char case is handled natively and efficiently.
- For Python 2, no equivalent of multi-char `str.translate` exists, so a per-character `str.replace` loop is used as a fallback only when `split` is longer than one character, preserving the original fast path for the common single-char case.

Related Issues

Fixes #9538

Tests

Added `test_text_to_word_sequence_multichar_split` and `test_text_to_word_sequence_unicode_multichar_split` to cover the new behaviour on both ASCII and unicode inputs.
messages.minimax:
Fix multi-character split string crash in text_to_word_sequence

The `text_to_word_sequence` function crashed with `ValueError: the first two maketrans arguments must have equal length` when using a split string longer than one character. This occurred because `maketrans(filters, split * len(filters))` requires the filter characters and replacement strings to have equal length, which is impossible when split has more than one character.

The fix uses a dictionary-based translation approach for Python 3 and falls back to a character-by-character replacement loop for Python 2 when a multi-character split is provided.

Fixes #9538.

docs: Fix inconsistent tensor shape documentation in convolutional layers

Standardize tensor shape descriptions across Conv1D, Conv2D, Conv3D, SeparableConv1D, and DepthwiseConv2D documentation. Replace inconsistent terminology (`length` → `steps`, `samples` → `batch`, `input_dim` → `channels`) and fix incorrect dimensions in SeparableConv1D docstring that referenced 2D shapes (height/width) instead of 1D shapes (steps). Also unify bracket formatting from square brackets to parentheses for consistency. These changes align the documentation with actual layer behavior and resolve issue #10737 where SeparableConv1D incorrectly listed width and height as input dimensions.
messages.claude:
docs: fix incorrect tensor shape documentation in convolutional layers

Replace inconsistent and incorrect dimension names in docstrings across Conv1D, Conv2D, Conv3D, SeparableConv1D, and DepthwiseConv2D:
- Conv1D: replace `length` with `steps` for the temporal dimension, and `batch_size`/`input_dim`/`new_steps` with `batch`/`channels`/`filters` to align with other layers
- Conv2D/Conv3D: replace `samples` with `batch` for consistency across input/output shape descriptions
- SeparableConv1D: replace `height`/`width` (incorrect for 1D input) with `steps` to match the actual 1D input shape `(batch, steps, channels)`/`(batch, channels, steps)`
- DepthwiseConv2D: replace square brackets `[...]` with parentheses `(...)` to match the convention used in other layers

Why: The SeparableConv1D documentation incorrectly listed `height` and `width` as input dimensions, which are 2D concepts that do not apply to 1D convolution (issue #10737). This is misleading for users and contradicts the corresponding TensorFlow docs. While fixing this, the related convolutional layer docstrings were also normalized so that batch is consistently referred to as `batch` rather than `samples` or `batch_size`, and tensor shape tuples use parentheses throughout. These changes improve documentation accuracy and consistency without altering any code behavior.

The previous message was confusing as it suggested calling the model on test data, which is not the standard way to build models in Keras 2.2.2+. The new message clearly explains that the model needs to be built and provides three concrete ways to do so: calling `build()`, calling `fit()` with data, or specifying `input_shape`/`batch_input_shape` in the first layer.

This change addresses issue #11217 where users found the original error message misleading compared to the more helpful error in Keras 2.1.6.
messages.claude:
fix: improve error message for model.summary() when model is not built

The previous error message ("This model has never been called, thus its
weights have not yet been created...") was confusing because it implied
the user needed to invoke the model on data, when in reality there are
multiple ways to build a model.

As reported in issue #11217, users calling model.summary() on an
unbuilt Sequential model were directed to "call it on some test data",
but this guidance was incomplete. The model can also be built by:
- calling build() explicitly
- calling fit() with some data
- specifying input_shape or batch_input_shape in the first layer for
  automatic build

The new message lists all available options, making it easier for users
to choose the approach that fits their workflow and restoring the
helpful behavior that existed in earlier Keras versions (2.1.6) where
the first-layer input_shape requirement was clearly surfaced.

context.issue:
Issue #11452: ImageDataGenerator inherits wrong class from TF 1.11, causing fit_generator to assume it isn't a Sequence
Tensorflow 1.11.0
Keras 2.2.4
Keras-Preprocessing 1.0.5
Ubuntu 16.04
Python 2.7.12

Example code:

```
from keras import models, layers
from keras_preprocessing.image import ImageDataGenerator
from keras_applications.imagenet_utils import preprocess_input

train_dir = '/tmp/workspace/Pet_Dataset/train/'
height, width, channels = (128, 128, 3)
batch_size=32

train_datagen = ImageDataGenerator(rescale=1.0/255)
train_generator = train_datagen.flow_from_directory(
              train_dir, target_size=(height, width),
              batch_size=batch_size, class_mode='categorical')

network = models.Sequential()
network.add(layers.Conv2D(32, (3, 3), activation='relu', input_shape=(height, width, channels)))
network.add(layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))
network.add(layers.Conv2D(64, (3, 3), activation='relu'))
network.add(layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))
network.add(layers.Conv2D(128, (3, 3), activation='relu'))
network.add(layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))
network.add(layers.Conv2D(256, (3, 3), activation='relu'))
network.add(layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D())
network.add(layers.Dense(train_generator.num_classes, activation='softmax'))

network.compile(optimizer='RMSProp',
                   loss='categorical_crossentropy',
                   metrics=['accuracy'])
network.summary()

history = network.fit_generator(train_generator, epochs=10) 
```

breaks with Tensorflow 1.11.0 with `ValueError: steps_per_epoch=None is only valid for a generator based on the keras.utils.Sequence class. Please specify steps_per_epoch or use the keras.utils.Sequence class.`. 

Tensorflow 1.10.0 and below works.

Furthermore, providing steps_per_epoch and applying multiprocessing with workers > 1:
```
history = network.fit_generator(train_generator, epochs=10, 
    steps_per_epoch=train_generator.n/batch_size,
    use_multiprocessing=True, workers=2)
```
causes a UserWarning about multiple workers duplicate data.

I think this is caused by wrong inheritance of ImageDataGenerator. 

When printing the exact class that is used in `keras_preprocessing/image.py`, I get `<class 'tensorflow.python.keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence'>`.

But `fit_generator()` checks if the generator is a subclass of `<class 'keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence'>`, so it seems to assume that the ImageDataGenerator instance is not of type Sequence, causing above problems.

messages.kimi:
fix: Improve type-check for Sequence to support TF 1.11+ compatibility (#11468)

Summary
Replace direct `isinstance(generator, Sequence)` checks with a new `is_sequence()` utility function that properly detects Sequence API compliance. This fixes compatibility issues with TensorFlow 1.11+ where `ImageDataGenerator` inherits from `tensorflow.python.keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence` instead of `keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence`.

Why
TensorFlow 1.11 changed the inheritance chain of `ImageDataGenerator` to use `tensorflow.python.keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence` instead of `keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence`. The existing `isinstance()` checks in `fit_generator`, `evaluate_generator`, and `predict_generator` failed to recognize these generators as valid Sequences, causing:
1. `ValueError` when `steps_per_epoch=None` (should be valid for Sequences)
2. Incorrect `UserWarning` about data duplication with multiprocessing
3. Validation data handling issues

The new `is_sequence()` function checks for Sequence API compliance via duck typing (checking for required methods) and a `use_sequence_api` attribute flag, making the detection robust against cross-module inheritance differences.

Changes
- Added `is_sequence()` utility function in `training_utils.py` with duck typing approach
- Added `use_sequence_api = True` attribute to `Sequence` base class
- Updated all `isinstance(generator, Sequence)` checks in `training_generator.py` to use `is_sequence()`
- Added integration test for `ImageDataGenerator` with `fit_generator`
- Fixed test skip conditions to only apply on Travis CI
messages.claude:
feat: support Sequence API detection beyond isinstance checks (#11468)

Summary

Decouple Sequence detection from a strict `isinstance(generator, Sequence)` check
in the generator-based training/evaluation/prediction paths. A new helper
`keras.engine.training_utils.is_sequence()` is introduced, which accepts an object
as a Sequence if it either opts in via the `use_sequence_api` flag or duck-types
the full `Sequence` interface (`set(dir(Sequence())` is a subset of `dir(seq)`).

The base `keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence` now exposes `use_sequence_api = True`,
and `fit_generator`/`evaluate_generator`/`predict_generator` use the new helper
instead of repeated `isinstance(..., Sequence)` calls.

Why

As reported in #11452, with TensorFlow 1.11 the standalone `keras_preprocessing`
package's `ImageDataGenerator` ends up inheriting from
`tensorflow.python.keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence` rather than
`keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence`. The two classes are structurally identical
but live in different modules, so Keras' own `isinstance(generator, Sequence)`
check returns `False`. This breaks `fit_generator`:

- `steps_per_epoch=None` raises `ValueError` even though the generator is
  genuinely Sequence-compatible, since Keras can no longer tell.
- When `use_multiprocessing=True` and `workers > 1`, users get a spurious
  UserWarning suggesting they switch to `keras.utils.Sequence`, and the
  `OrderedEnqueuer` path (which provides ordered, non-duplicating iteration)
  is silently skipped in favor of the plain generator path — reintroducing the
  data-duplication risk the Sequence API was designed to prevent.

The root cause is not a bug in `ImageDataGenerator` per se; it is that Keras
identifies Sequences by class identity rather than by behavior. Any third-party
or vendored Sequence (different module, same shape) hits the same wall.

The duck-typing + opt-in flag approach fixes this without forcing
`keras_preprocessing` (or downstream users) to import from
`keras.utils.data_utils` — they simply set `use_sequence_api = True` or
implement the full Sequence protocol. This restores correct `steps_per_epoch`
inference, the `OrderedEnqueuer` multiprocessing path, and silences the
misleading warning for genuine Sequences.

Accompanying changes:

- Re-enable the TensorFlow multiprocessing tests outside CI by gating the
  `pytest.mark.skipif` on `TRAVIS_PYTHON_VERSION` being set, so the new path
  gets exercised locally rather than being silently skipped.
- Add `tests/integration_tests/test_image_data_tasks.py::test_image_data_generator_training`
  to cover the `ImageDataGenerator` + `fit_generator`/`evaluate_generator` flow
  that regressed in #11452.
messages.minimax:
Fix is_sequence check to use duck-typing for Sequence API detection (#11468)

When TensorFlow 1.11+ is used, ImageDataGenerator inherits from tensorflow.python.keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence instead of keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence, causing isinstance(generator, Sequence) to return False even though ImageDataGenerator implements the full Sequence API. This broke fit_generator with steps_per_epoch=None and caused spurious warnings about use_multiprocessing duplicating data.

Instead of relying on isinstance, the check now uses a duck-typing approach: an object is considered a Sequence if it has use_sequence_api=True or has all the methods that keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence defines. The Sequence class itself is marked with use_sequence_api=True to serve as the canonical implementation.

context.issue:
Issue #11959: Suggesting keras.utils.*_utils packages should not be part of the official API
In general, all `keras.utils.*_utils.*` functions and classes that are documented on keras.io are available directly in `keras.utils` and documented as such. However there are a few discrepancies:
* `keras.utils.vis_utils.model_to_dot` is not available in `keras.utils`.
* `keras.utils.np_utils.to_categorical` sometimes appears in the documentation, instead of `keras.utils.to_categorical`.
* `keras.utils.io_utils.HDF5Matrix` sometimes appears in the documentation, instead of `keras.utils.HDF5Matrix`.

This introduces some confusion as to what is part of the official Keras API or not: in particular, are `keras.utils.*_utils` packages part of the Keras API or not? Possibly as a result of this confusion, tf.keras is not consistent with keras-team/keras, as it has no `tf.keras.utils.*_utils` packages, and is missing `model_to_dot` altogether. Arguably this is a tf.keras issue, but the fact that only three utility functions are placed in `keras.utils.*_utils` packages is surprising IMHO.

I will propose a PR to fix this by:
* Adding `model_to_dot` to `keras.utils`
* Fixing the documentation to remove all references to `keras.utils.*_utils` packages.

messages.claude:
fix: preserve input dtype in Lambda layer compute_output_shape

The Lambda layer's compute_output_shape creates a placeholder to infer
the output shape by calling the user function. Previously this
placeholder was always built with the default float32 dtype, ignoring
the actual dtype of the inputs the user declared (e.g. complex64 for
tf.fft2d, or float16).

This broke Lambda layers wrapping dtype-sensitive operations: the shape
inference path invoked the user function with a float32 placeholder,
causing ops that require a specific dtype (such as tf.fft2d, which only
accepts complex64/complex128) to raise a TypeError before the layer
ever ran on real data (issue #12121).

Fix by capturing the real input dtypes in Lambda.call (single or list
of tensors) and reusing them when constructing the inference
placeholder in compute_output_shape. The cached dtypes are stored in a
private _input_dtypes attribute to avoid changing the public API. Also
removes the now-unused conv_utils import and adds a test that a float16
input is preserved through the Lambda layer.
messages.kimi:
Looking at the code changes and the related issue, I can see:

1. What changed: The Lambda layer now preserves input dtypes when creating placeholders in `compute_output_shape`. It stores the input dtypes in `call()` and uses them when creating placeholders.

2. Why: Issue #12121 shows that when using `tf.fft.fft2d` (which requires complex64 input) in a Lambda layer, the layer was incorrectly creating float32 placeholders instead of preserving the original complex64 dtype, causing a TypeError.

3. Type: This is a fix - it fixes a bug where Lambda layers lose input dtype information.

Based on the reference examples (especially Example 1 which is nearly identical), here's the commit message:

fix: Preserve input dtypes in Lambda layer compute_output_shape (#12122)

The Lambda layer was losing input dtype information when computing output
shapes, causing errors with functions that require specific dtypes like
tf.fft.fft2d. When creating placeholders in compute_output_shape, the
layer now uses the stored input dtypes from the call() method instead of
defaulting to float32. This ensures that complex64 and other non-float
inputs are handled correctly.

context.issue:
Issue #10221: Weighted metrics are not loaded using load_model, only normal metrics are set
When using sample weights its important to use `weighted_metrics` instead of `metrics` to get the correct accuracy. However, the current implementation of load/save_model does not take these metrics in to account. 

Current implementations:

- `save_model` only saves metrics, see https://github.com/keras-team/keras/blob/master/keras/engine/saving.py#L144
- `load_model` only sets metrics, see https://github.com/keras-team/keras/blob/master/keras/engine/saving.py#L286

This problem only occurs after a loading a model and then trying to continue training (or using one of the weighted metrics). Ideally, the weighted metrics should also be saved and subsequently loaded.

messages.kimi:
fix: Add weighted_metrics support to model loading for backwards compatibility

Earlier versions of Keras did not properly save weighted_metrics, causing load_model to fail when the key was missing. This change uses .get() to safely retrieve weighted_metrics and passes them to model.compile(), ensuring models with weighted metrics can be loaded and continue training correctly. Fixes #10221.
messages.claude:
fix: Load weighted_metrics in load_model to preserve training config

Weighted metrics were not being restored when loading a saved model,
because `convert_custom_objects` only handled `loss` and `metrics`
while ignoring `weighted_metrics` from the training config. This meant
that after reloading a model and resuming training with sample weights,
the weighted metrics (e.g. weighted accuracy) were silently dropped,
producing incorrect evaluation results — the original issue #10221
reported that only normal metrics were set on the loaded model.

Use `training_config.get('weighted_metrics')` rather than a direct key
lookup so that models saved by older Keras versions — which never
dumped `weighted_metrics` — still load without a KeyError, preserving
backwards compatibility. The retrieved value is then forwarded to
`model.compile(..., weighted_metrics=weighted_metrics, ...)`, ensuring
the compiled model matches the configuration that was in effect when
the model was originally saved.
messages.minimax:
fix: load weighted_metrics when restoring model from save

When loading a model that was saved with weighted_metrics, the metrics were
restored but weighted_metrics were silently ignored. This caused incorrect
accuracy values when using sample weights, since weighted metrics must be
used instead of regular metrics in that context.

Use .get() for backwards compatibility with older Keras versions that did
not save weighted_metrics, avoiding KeyError on load.

context.issue:
Issue #12195: ValueError: Unable to create group (Name already exists) with model.save_weights()
This is a similar issue to https://github.com/keras-team/keras/issues/6005 but I believe it is caused by the way `h5py` defines groups. In particular, if a layer named `foo` is in a network after a layer named `foo/bar`, `h5py` throws an exception. But the same does not occur if `foo` comes first. To reproduce, see the snippet below.

```
from keras import layers, models

# This raises an exception.
input_layer = layers.Input((None, None, 3), name='test_input')
x = layers.Conv2D(1, 1, name='conv1/conv')(input_layer)
x = layers.BatchNormalization(name='conv1/bn')(x)
x = layers.Activation('relu', name='conv1')(x)
models.Model(inputs=input_layer, outputs=x).save_weights('test.h5')

# This doesn't raise an exception
input_layer = layers.Input((None, None, 3), name='test_input')
x = layers.Conv2D(1, 1, name='conv1')(input_layer)
x = layers.BatchNormalization(name='conv1/bn')(x)
x = layers.Activation('relu', name='conv1/relu')(x)
models.Model(inputs=input_layer, outputs=x).save_weights('test.h5')
```

Perhaps we could provide a more helpful error message in `keras/engine/saving.py`? For example, changing part of `save_weights_to_hdf5_group` to the following would help trace the offending layer name.

```
for layer in layers:
    try:
         g = group.create_group(layer.name)
    except ValueError:
         raise ValueError('An error occurred creating weights group for {0}.'.format(layer.name))
    symbolic_weights = layer.weights
    weight_values = K.batch_get_value(symbolic_weights)
```

Happy to create PR if this is helpful.

messages.kimi:
fix: Fix h5py group naming conflict when saving model weights

Sort model layers by name before saving to HDF5 to ensure group names are strictly growing. This prevents the "Name already exists" error that occurs when a layer name is a prefix of another layer name (e.g., 'conv1' vs 'conv1/conv') due to h5py's group naming behavior. Fixes #12195.
messages.claude:
fix: sort layers by name before saving to avoid h5py group naming conflicts (#13477)

When saving model weights to HDF5, h5py requires that group names be
strictly growing — a group `foo` cannot be created after a group
`foo/bar` already exists, because `foo/bar` implicitly creates `foo`
as an intermediate group. This caused a
`ValueError: Unable to create group (Name already exists)` in
`save_weights_to_hdf5_group` whenever a layer whose name was a prefix
of an earlier layer's name appeared later in the layer list (e.g. a
layer named `conv1` following a layer named `conv1/conv`), as
reported in issue #12195.

Sort the layers by `layer.name` before iterating so that group names
are created in lexicographic order, which guarantees that no prefix
group is created after one of its descendants. This is a minimal
change that preserves the existing weights format while making the
save path robust to layer naming patterns common in models that
reuse hierarchical names (e.g. `conv1/conv`, `conv1/bn`, `conv1`).

Also add a regression test `test_saving_group_naming_h5py` that
builds a model with a layer name that is a prefix of a previous
layer name, then exercises `save_weights` and `load_weights` to
ensure the round trip succeeds. Skip the flaky `test_mean_iou` with
a reference to #13477 for more context while the underlying
instability is investigated.
messages.minimax:
fix: sort layers by name to avoid h5py group naming collision (#12195)

When saving model weights to HDF5 format, layer names that are prefixes of
other layer names (e.g., 'conv1' and 'conv1/conv') cause h5py to throw
"Name already exists" errors. This occurs because h5py interprets these
as hierarchical groups. Fix by sorting layers alphabetically by name before
saving, ensuring group names grow strictly and avoid prefix collisions.
Add a regression test for this case.

messages.claude:
fix: raise ValueError for invalid output shapes in convolutional and locallyconnected layers

Add explicit validation in Conv1D/2D/3D and LocallyConnected1D/2D layers
to catch cases where downsampling (strides/kernel/padding) produces a
zero or negative output dimension. Previously, layers silently computed
invalid shapes, leading to cryptic downstream errors during build() or
execution rather than a clear failure at the source.

Why: When the configured kernel_size/strides exceed the input spatial
dimensions, the resulting output shape contains a non-positive value.
Without validation, this surfaced as an opaque AlreadyExistsError /
metric-registration error or a tensor-shape mismatch far from the
responsible layer (as reported in #15333, where reproducing the failure
locally was obstructed by unrelated metric-registration noise). Catching
the invalid shape at build() time gives users an actionable message
pointing at the offending layer and its input shape.

Also switches the locallyconnected test targets to one-hot encoded
vectors and uses CategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True) so that the
tests exercise the layer end-to-end without relying on sparse integer
targets that were incompatible with the configured loss.

Add explicit validation to raise clear error messages when downsampling produces zero or negative output dimensions. This helps users diagnose shape mismatches early during layer building rather than encountering cryptic errors later during model execution.

- Wrap compute_output_shape in Conv layers with try-except to catch ValueError and provide helpful guidance
- Add explicit checks in LocallyConnected1D and LocallyConnected2D build() methods for invalid output dimensions
- Add comprehensive test coverage for Conv1D, Conv2D, Conv3D, LocallyConnected1D, and LocallyConnected2D
- Fix test data preparation to use proper one-hot encoding for categorical crossentropy loss

Related to improving error handling and user experience when configuring convolution layers with incompatible input sizes and kernel/strides/padding combinations.
